hints: Focus on the Group 2 trend for reaction with water, think about how reactivity changes as you go down from Mg to Ba.
Remember that BaO forms the much more soluble hydroxide, so test-tube Q will contain far more dissolved $\text{OH}^-$ ions than test-tube P.
Connect solubility to pH, the more concentrated hydroxide solution will be more alkaline, so the other filtrate must have the lower pH.
walkthrough:
**Write what happens with water**

Both oxides are basic oxides and form hydroxides with water. Think of it simply as dissolving to give alkaline solutions.

$$\text{MgO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Mg(OH)}_2$$
$$\text{BaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ba(OH)}_2$$

**Apply the Group 2 reactivity trend**

Reactivity with water increases down Group 2. MgO is only sparingly soluble and reacts very slightly, while BaO reacts much more readily and vigorously.

So BaO is the oxide that reacts more readily with water.

**Link solubility to pH of the filtrate**

Solubility of Group 2 hydroxides also increases down the group. $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is much more soluble than $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$.

More dissolved hydroxide means higher $[\text{OH}^-]$ and higher pH. So filtrate Q (from BaO) has the higher pH, and filtrate P (from MgO) has the lower pH.

**Combine the two conclusions**

Oxide reacting more readily: BaO. Filtrate with lower pH: P in test-tube P. That combination matches one row in the table.

options.A: Correct. BaO is lower down Group 2 so it reacts more readily with water than MgO. Its hydroxide $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is also much more soluble, giving a higher $[\text{OH}^-]$ and higher pH in Q, leaving P (Mg filtrate) with the lower pH.
options.B: Half right, half wrong. BaO does react more readily, but Q cannot have the lower pH. Because $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is more soluble, Q is more alkaline with a higher pH, not lower.
options.C: Incorrect on reactivity. MgO is at the top of this pair in Group 2, so it is less reactive and less soluble. Students sometimes reverse the trend and think reactivity decreases down the group, but it increases.
options.D: Incorrect on both parts. MgO does not react more readily than BaO, and Q (barium hydroxide solution) is strongly alkaline so it has the higher pH, not the lower pH.
